excerpt: Ripcord uses document-scanning robots and AI to turn paper records into searchable, structured data. History, funding, the VASTEC merger, use cases and alternatives.
content:
Ripcord is a San Francisco company that digitises paper documents with robots and then extracts the data in them with AI. Its home page describes proprietary digitisation robotics that convert paper to digital files while keeping chain of custody, followed by AI that classifies documents and extracts, validates and enriches their data. The results are delivered through Canopy, its cloud content platform, or into a customer's existing systems. Ripcord's about page says the company was born at NASA research, and lists solutions for accounts receivable, energy, financial services, food and beverage, HR, insurance, manufacturing, the public sector and real estate.

Customers named on Ripcord's site include Coca-Cola bottlers, BP, UCLA, Waste Connections, MUFG Bank, Agilent, Daiwa Living and the US Internal Revenue Service. In 2022 Ripcord said it had advanced to phase two of an IRS pilot to digitise archived Form 709 gift-tax filings. Its case studies quote customer results, such as MUFG scanning 300 million pages; these are the company's own figures.

The company is venture-backed. On 16 April 2024 it announced $32 million in new funding from existing investors including Kleiner Perkins, GV (Google Ventures), Icon Ventures and Lux Capital, with Fujifilm Business Innovation, its joint-venture partner in Japan, taking equity. Ripcord said revenue grew 72% in 2023 and more than 95% in 2022, and that its generative-AI document platform, Docufai, entered beta in November 2023. In January 2025 it merged with VASTEC, a records digitisation and management provider with 18 years in government and enterprise work, to form Ripcord / VASTEC under CEO Sam Fahmy. Co-founder Kevin Hall is chief technology officer, and the advisers listed on the site include Apple co-founder Steve Wozniak.

Ripcord does not publish prices; projects are quoted after contacting the company.

This page is research, not a review. We have not used Ripcord; facts come from the company's own pages and press releases listed under Sources.

use_cases: Digitising large paper archives such as HR, insurance or tax files
Extracting structured data from invoices, contracts and forms
Making historical engineering or land records searchable
Moving records into a cloud content platform with chain of custody

fit: enterprises and agencies with millions of pages of paper records
regulated industries that need chain of custody for documents
operations teams that want data, not just scanned images
not_fit: small offices with a few boxes of paper, where a desktop scanner may do
buyers who want an instant online price
